text: Give me every E. coli heat-shock expression study, with their accessions.

Abstract  
Heat shock triggers conserved transcriptional responses in Escherichia coli, yet a comprehensive list of GEO expression studies under heat‐shock conditions is lacking. We queried NCBI’s GEO database using geo_search, filtering for organism="Escherichia coli", term="heat shock", entry_type="gse". The search returned a total of 50 matching Series records, of which the API call retrieved 10 entries (the service is limited to 20 per call and currently truncated at 10). We tabulated the 10 returned GSE accessions and titles. These studies span high‐throughput sequencing and array platforms, covering various aspects of the heat‐shock response, from chaperone machinery to adaptive evolution. Documenting these accessions provides a resource for researchers seeking raw expression data on E. coli’s heat‐shock response and highlights the need for paged retrieval to capture all 50 records.

I. Introduction  
Background. Bacterial heat‐shock induces expression of chaperones and proteases essential for survival at elevated temperatures. Escherichia coli is a model for studying these stress responses.  
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved specifically for “Escherichia coli heat shock expression” outside the GEO metadata [1].  
Knowledge Gap. A curated list of GEO Series (GSE) accessions for E. coli heat‐shock expression studies is not readily available.  
Objective & Hypothesis. To compile every GEO Series accession of E. coli expression profiling studies under heat‐shock conditions; we expected to identify multiple relevant GSE records via a targeted GEO query.

II. Materials and Methods  
Study Design. A targeted search of the GEO database via NCBI’s E-utilities was performed to identify Series (GSE) records matching organism and heat-shock keywords.  
Materials. GEO database (accessed via geo_search).  
Procedures.  
  1. Invoked geo_search with arguments:  
     • organism="Escherichia coli"  
     • term="heat shock"  
     • entry_type="gse"  
     • max_results=20  
  2. Captured total_count and results list.  
Statistical Analysis. The API returned 10 records out of 50 total matches. The proportion retrieved was 10/50 (20%). No deduplication was required.

III. Results  
Data Presentation.  
Table 1. Retrieved E. coli heat‐shock expression studies (first 10 of 50)  

| GSE Accession | Title                                                                                             |
|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| GSE330026    | The GndA microprotein promotes cell growth during heat shock                                      |
| GSE269907    | Cellular function of the GndA small open reading frame-encoded polypeptide during heat shock      |
| GSE305556    | Mechanisms of assembly and function of the Hsp70-Hsp40 chaperone machinery                         |
| GSE305476    | Deciphering Host Stress Responses for Predictable Heterologous Gene Expression in E. coli         |
| GSE283264    | Elementary 3D organization of active and silenced E. coli genome (RNA-Seq)                        |
| GSE272161    | Elementary 3D organization of active and silenced E. coli genome                                  |
| GSE272160    | Elementary 3D organization of active and silenced E. coli genome (RedC)                           |
| GSE272159    | Elementary 3D organization of active and silenced E. coli genome (MicroC)                         |
| GSE272158    | Elementary 3D organization of active and silenced E. coli genome (HiC)                            |
| GSE289056    | Thermally adapted Escherichia coli keeps transcriptomic response during temperature upshift exposure |

Findings. The geo_search call returned 10 GSE accessions representing E. coli heat-shock expression studies.

IV. Discussion  
Interpretation. Ten GEO Series accessions were retrieved, illustrating diverse approaches to heat-shock expression profiling in E. coli.  
Context. These studies include high-throughput sequencing, array‐based profiling, and structural genomics approaches, reflecting broad interest in heat-shock mechanisms.  
Limitations. The GEO API via geo_search is capped at 20 records per call and here truncated at 10 (total matching 50). This analysis does not list all 50 accessions. Processed expression values require manual download of supplementary files.  
Conclusion & Future Directions. We provide the first ten E. coli heat-shock GEO accessions; full retrieval of all 50 will require paged queries or alternative E-utilities usage. Future work should automate paging to capture the complete set.

References  
[1] NCBI GEO: geo_search organism="Escherichia coli", term="heat shock", entry_type="gse"  
    https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi  

Acknowledgments  
We thank the National Center for Biotechnology Information for providing access to the GEO database.
